name: Menkar
description: One of the Gaia benchmark stars, 76.4 parsecs away, 100 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Soubiran et al. (2024), A&A 682, A145, HD 18884: radius 100.206 +/- 3.384 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 12.2 +/- 0.04 mas (measured in 2006A&A...460..855W, as the table lists it) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

temperature.source: Soubiran et al. (2024), A&A 682, A145, HD 18884: effective temperature 3738 +/- 170 K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the paper's SED fit

gravity.source: Soubiran et al. (2024), A&A 682, A145, HD 18884: log g 0.66 +/- 0.07, the paper's own, from Newton's law with its radius and a mass from evolution models

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331, XHIP, HIP 14135: RV -26.08 +/- 0.02 km/s (quality A)

distance.source: Soubiran et al. (2024), A&A 682, A145, HD 18884: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with, 13.09 +/- 0.44 mas, inverted

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

text.card: One of the Gaia benchmark stars, 76 parsecs away: 100 times the Sun's width and 1,764 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 12.2 milliarcseconds, which gives 100.206 solar radii and 3,738 K at its surface.
text.locator: The catalogue's table, HD 18884: limb-darkened diameter, parallax, Teff, luminosity, radius, log g
